author: maintainer-agent

patch.value:
## Question
The product target is thousands of agents working the same workspace across many branches, merging without conflict or loss. Today that is delivered by field-aware three-way merge drivers plus history union and reanchoring. Those are correct for the divergence patterns tested. The open question is whether they remain correct — and remain conflict-free rather than merely correct — as branch count and divergence depth grow.

## Tension
Convergent replicated state buys order-independent merge by construction, which is exactly the property the merge conformance suite is being built to assert. It costs metadata weight in every record and it works against the plain-text, human-readable, git-diffable storage property that is a deliberate product commitment.

## Constraint that must be respected
Storage stays human-readable and git-native. Any convergence mechanism that turns items into opaque blobs is rejected on that ground alone, regardless of its theoretical merits.

## Evidence this decision waits on
Measured conflict rates from the merge conformance property suite at increasing branch counts, and invariant violations found by the deterministic simulation harness. Deciding before that evidence exists would be a preference, not a decision.
ADR: convergence model for concurrent workspaces — field-level merge semantics versus conflict-free replicated state at thousands of agents

The decision states the concurrency and divergence regime under which field-aware three-way merge is proven sufficient, with measured evidence; Rejected alternatives are recorded with their reasons, including full conflict-free replicated data types and operation-log-only storage; Any adopted change states its format_version and migration implications and its effect on the plain-text, git-diffable storage property; The decision names the acceptance evidence source — the merge conformance suite and the simulation harness — rather than asserting a position
Decide, with evidence, whether field-aware three-way merge is sufficient at the stated concurrency target or whether convergent replicated state is required

The shipped merge drivers resolve conflicts correctly for the concurrency levels observed so far. Whether they still do at thousands of simultaneous agents across many branches is an open question that silently constrains the federation and scale milestones.

Determines the storage format's long-term shape. Adopting convergent replicated state later is a format migration; adopting it never is a ceiling on concurrency. Both are expensive to discover by accident.
A recorded decision with the rejected alternatives, the evidence that decided it, and the format_version implications stated explicitly.

The merge-safety program has closed and federation is on the roadmap. The decision is cheapest before the GA contract freezes the storage format policy and while a simulation harness can still generate the evidence.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Measured convergence regime (2026-08-02, pm 2026.8.2, sandbox tracker, installed merge drivers). Union collections converge: the eleven ITEM_UNION_COLLECTION_FIELDS merge by element identity and are byte-identical in every direction and application order tested. Scalars do not: with branches A and B each rewriting description, priority, estimated_minutes and assignee, A<-B retains all four of A's values and B<-A retains all four of B's, because scalar three-way always resolves toward the merging side (preferred: ours). The merge is associative — A<-B<-C and A<-C<-B agree — so the failure is commutativity alone, and the two non-commuting directions are exactly the fleet's two: agent merges main into branch, integrator merges branch into main. Both merged workspaces report validate ok:true after git add and history-repair, and neither carries any recorded signal that the other exists. Identity has the same shape: two branches that mint one id produce one fused document with two create entries, and storage integrity only reports it when the two items had different types. Filed as pm-dlx7v7 (product), pm-1tns7o (the property suite that misses the class), pm-qx95lz (identity fusion); this decision is now blocked_by all three so the model is chosen against measurement rather than assertion.
